title: G. M. Kraslavaky, Suspected Soviet Agent

page_data.en:
C.K.Y. (c)
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
S. 2, Special Branch.
REPORT
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE. File No. REGISTRY No. S. B. D. 3017 Date 29 / 10 35）
Date October 28. 1935.

Subject G.M. Kraslavsky, Suspected Soviet Agent.

Made by D.S. Tcheremshansky. Forwarded by D.S.J. Coym

G.M. Kraslavsky, Suspected Soviet Agent, Soviet
citizen of Jewish origin, lawyer by profession, arrived in
Shanghai from Manchuria during the autumn of 1931 and soon
afterwards established a lawyer office at No.74 Szechuen Road.
He holds a Soviet passport No. R.6943 and on September 23, 1931
registered himself with the Chinese Authorities as a Soviet
citizen. In 1931 Kraslavsky resided together with M.M.
Shvetz, clerk in the employ of Dalbank (Far Eastern Bank).
For some time Kraslavsky worked in partnership with one M.E.
* A. 5714
Gilcher, a Russian lawyer of Jewish origin connected with
Soviet circles, who for some time was acting as legal adviser
to the United Petroleum Trust of U.S.S.R. In December, 1933
Kraslavsky severed partnership with Gilcher and established
his own office at No.38 Avenue Edward VII, Rooms 212/213.
Kraslavsky is reputed to be a trusted Soviet lawyer and has
many friends among local Soviet agents and employees.
Kraslavsky's late elder brother was formerly a member of a
Soviet Spy Organization on the Chinese Eastern Railway (known as
the "Shumsky and Vatchak" organization, the name of two leaders)
and during a raid on his house made by the Chinese Police in
February 1929 he committed suicide by shooting himself. His
younger brother, Mr. Leo S. Kraslavsky, age 27, a Soviet
A. 6914
citizen born in Melitopol, arrived in Shanghai on 29.8.35 by
s.s. "Dairen Maru" together with his wife, Mrs. Nellie G.
Kraslavsky, age 21, born in Manchuria. L.S. Kraslavsky
is employed with the Shanghai Leather Products Co., No.899
Avenue Joffre Apt. 37, and his wife works in the office of
G.M. Kraslavsky.

A relative of G.M. Kraslavsky, one Pavel Tsaman

Subject (in full) G. L. Kraslavsky, suspected Soviet Agent.

Made by D.S. Tcheremshansky. Forwarded by （签名）

（左侧批注：
See also
D. 5914.

D. 6222）

Information has been received to the effect that
G. L. Kraslavsky who is residing at flat 20, Park Apartments,
455 Rue Lafayette together with M. Shwetz, a clerk in the
employ of the local branch of "Dalbank", is a suspected Soviet
agent.

He is a Russian Jew and arrived in Shanghai from
Manchuria about four months ago. He is a lawyer by profession
and since October 15, 1931, he has been occupying an office at
74 Szechuen Road. He holds Soviet passport R.6943, and
registered with the Chinese Authorities on September 23, 1931
as a Soviet citizen.

His brother was formerly a member of a Soviet Spy
Organization on Chinese Eastern Railway (known as the "Sumsky
and Vetchak" case, the name of the two leaders) and during a
raid on his house made by the Chinese Police in February 1929,
he committed suicide by shooting himself.

（签名：G. Tcheremshansky）
D. S.

Officer i/c Special Branch.
